about: M2 role table: one row per ragdoll body role on the 106-joint (Mixamo-named) skeleton. Every number carries a source tag: HQ = Hellish Quart (docs/parts-lab/hellish-quart/data/physics.json, median of the 25+ fighters), HS = Half Sword Willie_PhysicsAsset_Capsules (docs/parts-lab/half-sword/data/hs-compare), GG = Gladio and Glory study (docs/STUDY-gladio-combat.md), own = starting value of ours, to tune in M4. Tools/ragdoll-gen.mjs turns this table plus one body_measure row into a ragdoll row. Armour never blocks a dismemberment (Dom, 2026-10-25): armour_tiers carry a dismember_threshold_modifier number, not a block flag; the generator lints any key that looks like a block.

motor.sk_note: M1 harness: stiffness = SK x subtree mass x 9.81 x 0.15 m arm (N*m/rad); damping = 2 x 0.8 x sqrt(K x subtree mass x 0.15^2). SK 40 was the value that held the Mixamo fight-idle pose to 4.6 degrees in Jolt (docs/parts-lab/physics/m1-bakeoff/RECEIPT.md).
motor.inertia_note: M1 finding: torso capsules need 8x inertia or the joint springs blow up at 60 Hz

motor.root: hips follow the animation as a kinematic body while the character is alive and are released on death (M1 finding)

solver.scope: thrown weapons and cuts only, inside the 60 Hz sim

stiffness_by_state.note: defaults for the motor strength scale per state; they will live on clip tags later (Strategy addendum 2026-10-25)

part_mechanics.formula: tip_speed_m_s = reach_m * angular_speed_rad_s (from the clip); strength follows from mass_kg * tip_speed; reach_m is the length of the part's chain to its tip
part_mechanics.note: every role row carries length_m, mass_kg and reach_m, measured per body from the measure row, so a dwarf, a reference body and a giant differ (Strategy addendum 2026-10-25, experiment 1: tip-speed histogram per body size)

severable.about: Six severable units that detach a part, plus two visual-only units (head_split, belly_open) that only switch cut-face meshes on (Half Sword Severable_BodyParts_Enum / HQ chopped heads). The corpse-cut is the loot mechanic: the player taps a part on a dead body, the finisher cut plays, physics detaches the part WITH its gear. Each unit names the role whose parent joint is removed, the roles that go with it, and the gear slots attached to it. The head is the template: the same fields serve all six.

units.note: the neck stump stays on the torso (neck role + neck slot gear stays unless a coif: see armour slot neck)
a waist cut: the upper body goes with everything attached above the cut; hips and legs stay as the root piece

VISUAL-ONLY (V1 Split Crown, docs/CUT-CONTRACT.md Optional cuts): shows the cut faces of the two head halves of a cut GLB made with --head-split. No capsule or joint is removed, no mass moves, the ragdoll lives on. cap_role is the part the event points at.

VISUAL-ONLY (V1 Opened): shows the wound decal of a cut GLB made with --belly-open. It removes no geometry and detaches nothing; no mass moves, the ragdoll lives on. cap_role is the part the event points at.

motor_strength_ramp.source: HQ killDuration 1 and Strategy M3 (1 to 0.01 over 1 s)

armour_tiers.about: Per armour tier and body slot. NO block field exists or is allowed (Dom 2026-10-25: armour raises the force needed to dismember and cuts damage; a hard enough blow still takes the head off, helmet and all, and the helmet flies off as a prop). Numbers are starting values, own, derived in shape from the HS rating ladder and the three-games document section 4; tune in M4. Design check for M4: every dismember-capable weapon class must be able to exceed 2.5x the dismember base, or top armour is a block in practice.

neck.note: a mail coif or gorget follows the head

design_check_ratio.rule: for every dismember-capable weapon class, its top attainable blow strength must exceed this ratio times the dismember base, or top armour is a block in practice (three-games doc section 4; Strategy addendum)
